claim.text: Fixing exact represented complex input tensors isolates cross-runtime solver reproducibility from version-sensitive random/QR input generation in Sionna LMMSE conditioning tests.
claim.scope: Six frozen synthetic source/transported complex tensor cases, two CPU PyTorch runtimes, two whitening modes, three repeats.
assumptions: same Sionna implementation and exact serialized input bits
conditions selected from historical deterministic generator
forbidden_promotions: Do not infer general reproducibility on arbitrary CPUs or GPUs
Do not attribute historical run variation uniquely to PyTorch version
Do not infer physical 6G sensitivity or BER/SER changes
Do not turn malformed finite-precision covariance tensors into counterexamples to an exact SPD theorem

specification.intended_object: Byte-identical original (y,H,S), transported (y',H',S'), and W tensors in a linear Gaussian LMMSE model.
invariants: SHA256 of every serialized input tensor matches fixture entry
Same fixture SHA256 across both runtimes
Within-runtime output bytes stable across three repeats per fixture/mode
Exact algebraic posterior invariance conditional on SPD and invertible transform

double precision 2x2 moderate condition source and transport

metric.units: SHA equality boolean; Cholesky info integer; error complex LMMSE estimate or effective-noise variance

Replay exact original and transported inputs rather than recomputing transport
Compare 3.11/2.9.1 vs 3.13/2.10.0 and repeat thrice each
Record recomputed WSW* mismatch separately from frozen input

Two whitening implementation paths, with and without Cholesky

matched_baselines: Same committed fixture and Sionna code on two CPU Torch runtimes
negative_controls: Three previously Cholesky-problem single precision high-condition transformations: expect raw failures to be reported, not suppressed
controls.compute_parity: Both jobs use single CPU thread, three repeated passes of identical input tensors; no performance comparison
controls.parameter_parity: Same six cases, whitening settings, array shapes and dtypes
controls.sampling_parity: No sampling during replay; all fixture bytes checked with SHA256
controls.data_access_parity: Both jobs read the same committed repository JSON fixture; no external runtime data

preregistration.prediction: Moderate controls remain within tolerances; fixed extreme failure classifications should reproduce across CPU versions if prior drift came from generated inputs
preregistration.primary_metric: Exact fixture digest and per-tensor hash identity followed by stability of output/failure classification by fixture and whitening mode
preregistration.uncertainty_method: Deterministic three-repeat observations on two hosted CPU environments; no population-level confidence bounds or cross-platform probability claim
preregistration.kill_condition: If fixture SHA or any tensor digest differs across jobs, cross-runtime comparisons are invalid; if moderate safe controls fail, retire the numerical-safe-region claim
preregistration.stop_condition: After frozen replay and documentation, no further upstream modification absent maintainer request or supported receiver trace
preregistration.promotion_rule: Promote only stable failure classification and moderate-condition observed tolerance for six selected byte-frozen fixtures. Retire portable bitwise-output equality since second run contradicts it.

result.observed: Frozen SHA-256-identical fixture replayed in two separate CI runs and both CPU PyTorch runtimes. All 12 fixture/mode failure classes match (nine finite, three nonfinite) with immediate threefold repeatability. First CI run: all nine finite original/transformed output pairs matched bytewise across versions; second: zero of nine matched. Between runs Python 3.13 kept 9/9 finite pairs bit-identical, whereas Python 3.11 changed 9/9. In the second run, recomputing W S W^H from frozen bytes matched the stored transported covariance for 6/6 cases in PyTorch2.10.0, zero of six in PyTorch2.9.1.
result.effect_size: 12/12 stable failure-class matches across versions and both runs; 9/9 then 0/9 finite output hash pairs equal across runtimes; 0/9 cross-run stable finite pair outputs in Python3.11, 9/9 in Python3.13. Each environment/run had 12/12 safe replay rows pass and 9 nonfinite extreme rows.
result.uncertainty: Two independent hosted runner runs, two CPU runtime combinations, three in-process repetitions each, six selected synthetic fixtures. Exact host CPU model/ISA and BLAS dispatch not matched; no statistical or RF population generalization.
retired_claims: Historical run-to-run failure-count variability necessarily reflects a PyTorch-version-dependent solver defect
A seeded random/QR fixture is equivalent to a byte-identical fixture across runtimes
Fixed represented input bytes guarantee bit-identical finite solver outputs across different hosted CPU runs
The earlier run variability can be attributed exclusively to non-identical QR-generated inputs
active_remainder: The two first/second replay runs differ in finite Python3.11 output bytes despite identical input fixture SHA; isolate processor model and CPU BLAS dispatch if operationally motivated
The historical generator's exact original inputs were not archived per run; cannot uniquely attribute its previous variation
Real-world receiver and GPU relevance not tested; stop absent upstream request
